messages:
customer-jane: Hi, POST /v1/score to https://svc.acme.internal returns 502 and sometimes curl says 'curl: (6) Could not resolve host: svc.acme.internal' — started after the VPC move this morning. Can someone help?

support_oncall: On it. Can you paste the output of `dig svc.acme.internal +trace` and `curl -v`? Also which VPC is this in (prod/dev)?

customer-jane: Prod VPC (vpc-prod-23). Here's dig from an affected EC2 in that VPC:
```
; <<>> DiG 9.11.3-1ubuntu1.15-Ubuntu <<>> svc.acme.internal +trace
;; global options: +cmd
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NXDOMAIN, id: 12345
;; flags: qr rd ra; QUERY: 1, ANSWER: 0, AUTHORITY: 1, ADDITIONAL: 1
;; AUTHORITY SECTION:
acme.internal.       60  IN  SOA ns-1.awsdns.com. awsdns-hostmaster.amazon.com. 1 7200 900 1209600 60

;; Received 81 bytes from 10.0.0.2#53(10.0.0.2) in 2 ms
```

customer-jane: curl -v shows Host resolved sometimes then 502, sometimes fails to resolve entirely.

support_oncall: Thanks — NXDOMAIN from the VPC resolver. Two quick checks: is the private hosted zone for svc.acme.internal associated with this VPC? And any recent Route53 changes?

devon: I can look. Checking Route53 PHZ associations now.

(devon pasted) devon: `aws route53 get-hosted-zone --id ZZZZZZZ` -> name: acme.internal., privateZone: true, VPCs: [vpc-dev-11, vpc-staging-5] (no vpc-prod-23)

maria: That'd explain NXDOMAIN — private hosted zone not attached to prod VPC. Why wasn't prod associated in the migration?

customer-jane: We assumed DNS would be global after the migration. Ops runbook didn't include cross-account PHZ association step.

support_oncall: Two ways to fix: 1) Associate the PHZ with vpc-prod-23 (if same account) via `associate-vpc-with-hosted-zone` OR 2) Create a Route53 Resolver inbound endpoint and add a cross-VPC rule in the prod account pointing to the account owning the PHZ. Which account owns the PHZ?

devon: PHZ is in the platform account (acct-111). Prod app is in customer acct (acct-222). So cross-account association needed. We apparently attempted a cross-account association last week but it failed due to missing permissions.

alex: Also note split-horizon risk: there is a public zone acme.internal? Not recommended. I see a public hosted zone `acme.internal.` exists in platform account too — that can cause the resolver to prefer public NS if misconfigured. But current NXDOMAIN indicates resolver didn't find the private records for prod.

support_oncall: Good catch. customer-jane, do you have outbound/egress allowlists on your VPC that might block Route53 Resolver IPs or AWS APIs? If the assoc call failed earlier it could be an IAM/Resolver issue.

customer-jane: We do have strict egress rules. Allowed IPs only to internal-nat and 10.0.0.0/8 for internal services. Could that break resolver traffic?

maria: Route53 Resolver endpoints use ENIs in the VPC — if your NACL/SGs block UDP/TCP 53 to the resolver inbound ENIs, you can get NXDOMAIN. Also cross-account association still requires the `route53resolver:AssociateResolverEndpoint` permissions and possibly peering of resolvers.

devon: Reproduced from my shell by creating a quick assoc in staging: when the PHZ isn't associated, `dig` returns NXDOMAIN and no additional answers; when assoc present, dig returns A records.

support_oncall: Action items: (1) platform team (devon/maria) to request cross-account association and confirm IAM role trust and `AssociateHostedZone` permissions, (2) prod infra (customer-jane) to allow Route53 Resolver traffic and ensure SG/NACL allow 53 and outbound access to platform account resolver ENIs if using resolver endpoints, (3) short-term workaround: update /etc/hosts on critical nodes or add conditional forwarder to VPC resolver rules.

devon: I'll open a ticket with platform to perform the cross-account association. Maria, can you check permission boundary on the PHZ?

maria: On it — checking now. Also noticed public hosted zone `acme.internal` exists in root account; that was probably created by mistake during an import. If we leave both public and private names identical and resolver rule precedence is wrong, machines could hit public NS and see no records. We'll clean that up after association.

customer-jane: For immediate relief, can we add a conditional forwarder rule in prod to forward `acme.internal` to the platform resolver IPs? We can then rollback when PHZ assoc is done.

alex: Yes, create a outbound resolver rule in prod: `aws route53resolver create-resolver-rule --creator-request-id tmp --domain-name acme.internal --rule-type FORWARD --target-ips Ip=10.2.3.5,Port=53` and associate with VPC. That forwards queries to platform resolver. Make sure SG allows it.

customer-jane: Trying the forwarder now...

(customer-jane pasted) customer-jane: `aws route53resolver associate-resolver-rule --resolver-rule-id rsl-abc --vpc-id vpc-prod-23` -> association succeeded :eyes:

(customer-jane pasted dig) customer-jane: dig now returns `10.4.5.6` for svc.acme.internal — applications can resolve, testing traffic.

support_oncall: Nice. Can you run a quick end-to-end test hitting the service?

customer-jane: Ran curl, got 200 for a couple of calls. Latency slightly higher due to forwarding but acceptable.

maria: I'll follow up with platform to finish cross-account PHZ association and remove the temporary forwarder. We'll also remove the accidental public hosted zone `acme.internal` to avoid split-horizon.

devon: I'll make a runbook update for VPC migrations that includes: verify PHZ associations, confirm resolver rules, and check egress allowlists/SGs for resolver traffic.

support_oncall: Great. Marking thread as monitoring — please update when platform association is complete so we can close. :thumbsup:

customer-jane: Will do, thanks everyone.

dns-bot: Automated reminder: file #INC-4567 created for PHZ cross-account association.

customer-jane: Logged in ticket, will follow. Last check: dig stable for 10 minutes, no NXDOMAIN seen.

support_oncall: Closing here after final confirmation from platform.
